chunks: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Abd al-Rahman al-Ju'fi, who said:

I used to go to Ibn Abi Layla regarding our inheritances so that he would distribute them, and there was a 'habis' (detention/withholding) in it, so he would delay/deny me. When it became prolonged, I complained about him to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: 'Does he not know that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ordered the release of the 'habis' and the execution of the inheritances?' He said: So I went to him, and he did as he used to do. I said to him: 'I have complained about you to Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him).' He said to me: 'So-and-so and so-and-so' (quoting what I had said). Ibn Abi Layla swore me that he had said that, so I swore to him, and he ruled in my favor with that.

key_terms.انْفَاذِ الْمَوَارِيثِ: The execution or implementation of the inheritance distribution
key_terms.حَبِيسٌ: A detention or withholding of property/estate by a judge or authority
key_terms.رَدِّ الْحَبِيسِ: The release or lifting of the withholding/detention

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on withholding inheritance distribution (habis) according to the Prophet's command?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the practical application of the Prophet’s directive to prioritize the execution of inheritance shares over the retention of 'habis' (withheld estate) for minor heirs or debts. It highlights Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq’s role in resolving judicial delays by invoking prophetic precedent, thereby reinforcing the Shia legal principle that inheritance distribution should not be unduly prolonged. The narrative underscores the authority of the Imams in guiding contemporary jurists to align their rulings with established Sunnah.
